chunks: Ali ibn Mahziyar from Fadala from Aban from Mis'mam from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) who said:

My father used to consider for these two Sanctuaries what he did not consider for others, and he would say, 'Indeed, completing [the rituals] in them is among the reserved/accumulated [virtue/command].'
ai.seo_question: What is the special status of the two Sanctuaries according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) narrates that his father, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him), attributed a unique legal status to the two Sanctuaries (Mecca and Medina), emphasizing that the perfection of rituals within them is a 'reserved command' (al-amr al-madhkur). This highlights the Shia scholarly view that the sanctity of these cities imposes specific, elevated obligations or virtues upon pilgrims, distinguishing them from other regions in Islamic jurisprudence.
